direction: Run a batched population search from genuinely different topologies, using matrixized NumPy rather than many sequential expensive trials: maintain a batch of 24–32 configurations of shape $(B,76,15)$ initialized from random points, Thomson/Riesz-energy minimizers, perturbed records, and records with 15-point random subsets completely resampled, and optimize all replicas simultaneously with einsum-computed log-sum-exp gradients at several temperatures, periodically swapping configurations between temperatures when a hotter replica finds a lower smoothed objective. Anneal each replica from $\beta=30$ to $\beta=500$, discard all but the best three distinct contact graphs—measured by their sets of pairs within 0.005 of the maximum—and give each survivor at most 15 seconds of LP polishing. Enforce a hard internal deadline of 160 seconds and always keep a normalized copy of the loaded record as a fallback, avoiding the repeated whole-program timeouts seen previously.

idea: Global basin-hopping with hole reinsertion plus fast two-stage repulsion annealing (soft-max Adam then hard max-pair descent) and no LP to stay in budget while rebalancing contacts.

Balanced basin-hopping that walks away from the jammed core via worst-point-weighted soft-max annealing with uniform-spreading term plus sequential hole-optimized kill-and-fill, using a wandering current state with sideways acceptance instead of greedy restart-from-best.
Symmetric C15 orbit search with antipodal and signed variants optimized derivative-free, then unconstrained LSE annealing release plus hole-reinsertion basin-hopping and capped LP polish.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained orbit constructions, which automatically prevent rattlers and unequal contact degrees: let $G$ be the cyclic coordinate-permutation group $C_{15}$ in $\mathbb R^{15}$, take five generic $G$-orbits of 15 points each plus the $G$-fixed unit vector $(1,\ldots,1)/\sqrt{15}$, giving exactly 76 points parameterized by only five seed vectors. Optimize those seeds, normalized and optimized on their tangent spaces, using an annealed log-sum-exp approximation to the maximum cosine, followed by unconstrained release of all 76 points and a final LP polish; also try the analogous construction with signed cyclic shifts and with 38 antipodally generated seed pairs reduced by a global rotation. Because every orbit point has symmetry-equivalent contacts, any good symmetric critical point has the balanced contact structure absent from the current record and may lie in a completely different basin.

idea: Equitable target-feasibility continuation that forces all per-point maxima toward a common decreasing level with projected Adam plus brief LP checks.
direction: Use target-feasibility continuation to force rattlers to become load-bearing: define per-point maxima $m_i=\max_{j\ne i}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle$ and optimize $F_t=\sum_i \mathrm{softplus}(80(m_i-t))^2+\sum_i \max(0,t-0.002-m_i)^2$, where the second term pulls rattlers toward, but not beyond, the active level. Start at $t=0.16826349$, solve with projected Adam/L-BFGS on tangent vectors, then decrease $t$ in steps of $0.00025$–$0.0005$, warm-starting each stage and accepting a stage only if $\max_i m_i\le t+10^{-5}$ after a brief LP polish. This explicitly seeks an equitable configuration in which all 76 row-maxima approach a common lower value, instead of merely minimizing the global maximum while allowing 11 points to remain irrelevant.

idea: Core surgery deleting the most over-contacted points, hinge-plus-softmax re-optimization of the reduced core, greedy 50k-sample hole reinsertion with batch refinement and local gradient polish, then one capped global LP.
direction: Perform core surgery rather than rattler surgery: compute contacts at slack $<10^{-9}$, rank points by contact degree and by the sum of their near-maximal cosines, delete 6–10 of the worst core points, and re-optimize the remaining 66–70 points with a hinge objective $\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-0.164)^2$ plus a soft-max term until those points are comfortably below the record. Reinsert the deleted points one at a time, choosing each new point by sampling at least 50,000 random sphere candidates, refining the best 20 by local hole maximization, then running a short tangent-space LP polish restricted to the inserted point and its 20 nearest neighbours; after all insertions use one final global LP polish capped at 20 seconds. Try deletion sets of size 6, 8 and 10 within a strict 165-second budget, retaining any intermediate configuration that beats 0.168263492524.

idea: Optimize five cyclic generators plus all-ones vector with L-BFGS-B on log-sum-exp surrogates of increasing sharpness, then break symmetry with annealed soft-max repulsion and greedy contact descent.
direction: Search first in a symmetry-constrained, automatically contact-balanced family: use the cyclic group \(C_{15}\) acting by cyclic permutation of the 15 coordinates, take five generic generator vectors and expand each into its 15 cyclic shifts to give 75 points, and add the normalized all-ones vector as the 76th point. Optimize only the five generators with L-BFGS-B on a log-sum-exp surrogate for the expanded code, increasing \(\beta\) through \(50,150,450\) and pulling the expanded gradient back to the generators by summing over their cyclic preimages; reject or penalize generators whose orbits nearly collide. After this equal-orbit optimization, release the symmetry by allowing all 76 points to move independently, first with a short soft-max anneal and then with LP polish, so the symmetric configuration serves as a new basin rather than as the final answer.

idea: Break the over-jammed core by deleting high-contact points into largest-hole positions and re-annealing with fast vectorized soft-max repulsion in a basin-hopping walk without LP.
Balance overloaded core versus rattlers with row-balanced soft-max repulsion annealing plus hole-optimized reinsertion, LP-free for speed.
Contact-Jacobian floppy-mode surgery with svds null-space moves plus LSE-Adam anneal and short LP polish.
direction: Perform contact-Jacobian floppy-mode surgery instead of random shaking: from `best.npy`, form the active set of pairs with slack below \(10^{-7}\), build the tangent-space Jacobian whose \((i,j)\) row has blocks \(x_j-cx_i\) at \(i\) and \(x_i-cx_j\) at \(j\), project out each point’s radial direction, and compute its smallest singular vectors with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. Move all points simultaneously along combinations of the lowest 5–20 singular modes with amplitudes \(0.03,0.06,0.12,0.24\), optionally adding larger motion to rattlers, then run a fast vectorized log-sum-exp Adam anneal (\(\beta=40\to400\), about 1500 steps) and at most 20 seconds of trust-region LP polish. Accept only configurations whose polished score improves, otherwise try another mode combination; enforce a hard internal deadline of 165 seconds and time-check every 32 iterations.

idea: Delete rattlers plus hub points to free a 50-56 point core, anneal the core to low max-cosine, then greedily reinsert points into largest holes with massive sampling plus hole refinement and repolish.
direction: Delete and rebuild a substantial fraction of the code rather than only its rattlers: remove the 11 rattlers plus 9–15 of the highest-contact hub points, leaving a 50–56 point core, and optimize that core aggressively with annealed soft-max Adam until its maximum is preferably below \(0.15\), because the deleted points cannot be reinserted successfully unless the core creates real space. Sequentially reinsert one deleted point at a time by sampling at least 50,000 sphere candidates, selecting the candidate minimizing its maximum cosine to the current code, locally optimizing that hole for 200 tangent-gradient steps, inserting it, and re-polishing the whole growing code for 300–500 steps after every insertion. Try removal sizes \(16,20,24,28\) in separate time-boxed runs, keep the best complete 76-point result, and reserve the last 20 seconds only for a short LP polish of the incumbent.

direction: Run a diversity-preserving global search that does not start every trial from the record: generate 12–16 independent starts from random Gaussian points, perturbed unions of two lower-dimensional spherical codes embedded into orthogonal coordinate blocks, and cyclic-orbit configurations, then optimize each for only 6–8 seconds using fully vectorized tangent Adam on a log-sum-exp objective. Characterize every result by its sorted Gram-matrix eigenvalues, contact-degree histogram, and number of rattlers, cluster near-duplicates, and retain the best representative from each distinct cluster rather than merely the few lowest scores. Give only the best three diverse representatives a 15-second LP polish each, return the overall best, and use explicit `time.time()` checks throughout so `solve()` finishes by about 165 seconds without invoking expensive LP inside the exploratory loop.

idea: Core-surgery basin hopping that removes worst-pair and overloaded jammed points, reinserts them into sampled largest holes with sphere-refined minimax placement, then rebalances with normalized soft-max tangential annealing and exact worst-pair descent.
Escape the jammed record along Jacobian null/floppy modes from a single SVD then re-descend filtered low-contact trials with softmax annealing and capped trust-region LP polish.
direction: Compute a rigidity-matrix floppy-mode escape, but with strict cheap linear algebra: build the Jacobian $A$ of all pairs with slack $<10^{-7}$ in a tangent basis (about $460\times1064$), take one NumPy SVD, and generate trial displacements as random combinations of right-singular vectors with singular value below $10^{-3}$ times the largest, at amplitudes 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10 in both signs. Score each trial by exact maximum and by contact count, retaining configurations whose maximum rises by at most 0.003 but whose contact count falls below ~300, then re-descend those with annealed softmax Adam and a short capped LP polish. Cap the SVD to one call, check time every loop, use a 150s deadline, and return the incumbent if no escaped basin improves.

idea: Build a C15-symmetric basin from five 15-orbits plus the all-ones pole and optimize the five seeds with L-BFGS-B on log-sum-exp, then break symmetry with tangent Adam and a time-capped linearized minimax polish.
direction: Build a genuinely different symmetric basin from scratch, ignoring the record except as a fallback: use five generic orbits of size 15 under cyclic coordinate permutation in $\mathbb{R}^{15}$, plus the all-ones pole, giving $5\cdot15+1=76$ points parameterized by only five seed vectors. Optimize the seeds with SciPy L-BFGS-B on a log-sum-exp objective (beta 200–400) over all within- and between-orbit cosines, trying 6–8 random seeds for at most 15s each, then release all coordinates with 1500 steps of tangent Adam and a final 15s capped LP polish. Keep the best released configuration under a 155s deadline, and only return it if it beats simply returning `best.npy`.

idea: Rebalance the over-constrained jam by hole-optimized reinsertion of rattlers and overloaded hubs plus whitening to isotropize covariance, followed by fast projected log-sum-exp repulsion annealing without LP.
Balanced basin-hopping that teleports overloaded hubs and rattlers into refined holes, whitens covariance toward isotropy, then anneals LSE repulsion with isotropy penalty using tangent descent.
Hub-centroid shedding plus hole-teleported rattlers followed by balance-regularized Adam annealing and capped LP polish
direction: Perform explicit contact-load rebalancing surgery on hubs: choose the 6 points with the most contacts, compute their tight-neighbour sets (slack $<10^{-7}$), and move each hub a distance 0.05–0.15 along the negative centroid of its neighbours' tangent directions so it sheds roughly half its contacts, simultaneously teleporting 3–6 rattlers into the largest holes adjacent to those hubs. Then anneal with an augmented objective, log-sum-exp of pair cosines plus $\lambda\sum_i (\text{soft-contact-load}_i-\bar L)^2$ plus $\mu\|X^TX-(76/15)I\|_F^2$, with $\lambda,\mu$ decayed from $10^{-2}$ to 0 over 2000 Adam steps, followed by a 15s capped LP polish. Repeat for a few deterministic hub choices under a 150s deadline, keeping any result whose contact-degree variance drops sharply even before its score beats the record.

idea: Core-continuation with annealed LSE-Adam on the 65-point non-rattler core then greedy hole reinsertion with local Adam and capped trust-region LP polish under a slowly raised threshold.
direction: Use $N$-continuation on the non-rattler core instead of perturbing all 76 points: delete the 11 zero-contact points, optimize the remaining 65-point core alone with annealed log-sum-exp Adam (beta 50→600, 3000 steps) until its internal maximum is well below the record, then reinsert points one at a time by sampling 20000 random hole candidates against the current set, refining the best hole by 100 softmax steps, and locally re-optimizing only the inserted point plus neighbours with cosine $>0.05$ while freezing the rest. After each insertion, run a capped LP polish (at most 1500 constraints, 10s) and only accept the insertion if the global maximum stays below a slowly raised threshold starting at the core optimum; enforce a hard 150s internal deadline and return the best complete 76-point set found, falling back to `best.npy`.

idea: Cyclic C15 orbit basin with L-BFGS-B log-sum-exp seed optimization then full release Adam anneal and capped LP polish.
direction: Build a genuinely different symmetric basin from scratch, ignoring the record except as a fallback: use five generic orbits of size 15 under cyclic coordinate permutation in $\mathbb{R}^{15}$, plus the all-ones pole, giving $5\cdot15+1=76$ points parameterized by only five seed vectors. Optimize the seeds with SciPy L-BFGS-B on a log-sum-exp objective (beta 200–400) over all within- and between-orbit cosines, trying 6–8 random seeds for at most 15s each, then release all coordinates with 1500 steps of tangent Adam and a final 15s capped LP polish. Keep the best released configuration under a 155s deadline, and only return it if it beats simply returning `best.npy`.

idea: N-continuation on the 65-point non-rattler core with annealed LSE-Adam then greedy hole reinsertion with local subset anneal and capped LP polish.
direction: Use $N$-continuation on the non-rattler core instead of perturbing all 76 points: delete the 11 zero-contact points, optimize the remaining 65-point core alone with annealed log-sum-exp Adam (beta 50→600, 3000 steps) until its internal maximum is well below the record, then reinsert points one at a time by sampling 20000 random hole candidates against the current set, refining the best hole by 100 softmax steps, and locally re-optimizing only the inserted point plus neighbours with cosine $>0.05$ while freezing the rest. After each insertion, run a capped LP polish (at most 1500 constraints, 10s) and only accept the insertion if the global maximum stays below a slowly raised threshold starting at the core optimum; enforce a hard 150s internal deadline and return the best complete 76-point set found, falling back to `best.npy`.

idea: Balanced basin-hopping that escapes the over-jammed core by deleting hub points, reinserting hole-optimized vectors, mild covariance whitening toward isotropy, and two-phase softmax repulsion annealing without any LP.
